title: Wrap the DB write in StudyDayConfigScreen._toggleDay with catch/log and a consistent mounted guard
why: _toggleDay runs its DB lookup + db.studyDayConfigDao.upsertDayConfig(...) inside a detached `.then()` async closure with no surrounding try/catch and no caller awaiting the result — if upsertDayConfig throws (constraint violation, disk error), the failure is silently swallowed by the Future machinery with no AppLogger call and no user feedback (unlike the sync-push call three lines later, which IS wrapped in `on TutorWriteException catch`). The same closure calls `ref.invalidate(allDailyTasksProvider)` at line 288 with no `context.mounted` check, yet the SAME method DOES check `context.mounted` before the SnackBar at line 299 just after — an inconsistent, incomplete guard that leaves the earlier call exposed to a disposed-widget race if the user navigates away quickly after tapping a day toggle.
recommendation: Wrap the DB write in try/catch with an AppLogger.error call and user-facing feedback on failure; check `context.mounted` (or equivalent) before the `ref.invalidate` call, matching the guard already present for the SnackBar.
acceptance_criteria: A thrown exception from upsertDayConfig is logged via AppLogger and does not vanish silently.
ref.invalidate(allDailyTasksProvider) is only called when the widget is still mounted.

corrections: The claim 'silently swallowed...no AppLogger call' is factually wrong: main.dart wraps runApp in runZonedGuarded, whose handler calls AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack) plus Crashlytics.recordError(fatal: true). The failure does surface — just mislabeled as a fatal crash rather than silently vanishing.

main.dart:15-34 wraps the app in runZonedGuarded; its handler calls AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack) AND Crashlytics.recordError(fatal:true) for any uncaught error in this unawaited .then() chain — the write's failure is not actually silent/log-less as claimed. Also, the cited 'good' catch at line 298 is itself log-less for non-permission-denied TutorWriteException codes.
